name: Dried Apricots
description: Dried apricots (Prunus armeniaca) are a nutrient-dense botanical concentrate, valued for their high electrolyte and trace mineral profile. By removing moisture, the concentration of potassium, iron, and carotenoids creates a highly functional fuel matrix that optimizes cardiovascular hemodynamics, hematopoiesis, and gastrointestinal transit.
macroIntro: A dense, slow-release carbohydrate architecture characterized by significant dietary fiber content and a negligible lipid footprint.
microIntro: A superior bioavailable micronutrient payload, specifically serving as a premier plant-based source of potassium and iron to reinforce systemic vascular and blood cell integrity.

healthBenefits: Vascular Hemodynamics: Exceptionally high potassium-to-sodium ratio facilitates arterial wall relaxation and blood pressure normalization.
Gastrointestinal Kinetics: Soluble fiber (pectin) acts as an effective prebiotic, accelerating bowel transit and inhibiting toxic stasis.
Hematopoiesis: Synergistic Iron and Copper profiling optimizes red blood cell production, mitigating tissue hypoxia and fatigue.
Ocular & Dermal Protection: Beta-Carotene and Vitamin E payloads create a robust antioxidant barrier against oxidative degradation.
precautionsIntro: Nutritional precision is required regarding glycemic density and industrial chemical processing:
precautions: Glycemic Index (GI) Management: Dehydration significantly concentrates saccharides per gram; intentional portion control is required for insulin-resistant individuals.

Preservative Exposure (SO2): Brightly colored commercial apricots may contain Sulfur Dioxide, a potential allergen triggering respiratory distress; naturally sun-dried (dark brown) variants are preferable.
Osmotic Digestive Effects: High fructose and fiber concentrations may induce transient osmotic diarrhea or bloating in individuals with sensitive gastrointestinal tracts or IBS.
